short: Thomas Cranmer was the first Protestant Archbishop of Canterbury and the principal architect of the Book of Common Prayer.
full:
Appointed Archbishop of Canterbury by Henry VIII, Thomas Cranmer provided the theological and legal arguments necessary for the king's divorce from Catherine of Aragon. While he cautiously advanced Protestant ideas during Henry's reign, it was under Edward VI that Cranmer fully transformed the English Church. He authored the first two editions of the *Book of Common Prayer*, replacing the Latin Mass with English liturgy and establishing the foundational doctrines of Anglicanism.

Following the accession of the Catholic Mary I, Cranmer was arrested for treason and heresy. After a long imprisonment, he yielded to intense pressure and signed several recantations of his Protestant faith. However, on the day of his execution in 1556, he dramatically renounced his recantations, famously thrusting his offending right hand into the fire first as he burned at the stake in Oxford.
